text:
ian_support: Hey team — customer AdVerve opened a ticket: after migrating traffic through their new NAT proxy they started seeing intermittent 429s. They say only some keys are affected and the 429s spike during short bursts. Attached sample response headers: `x-rw-request-id: rw_abc123`, `x-ratelimit-limit: 1200`, `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 1680000123`. They included this curl that reproduces it from their CI runner behind the proxy:

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-adverve-prod-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":20}'

ian_support: They also set `X-Forwarded-For: 52.18.23.11` (original client IP). Ticket claims the proxy rewrites source to the NAT IP 3.120.45.9.

maria: thanks, grabbing the ticket now. quick q — did they rotate keys or change projects during the migration?

ian_support: customer says no, same key and project id. Only noticeable change is the NAT IP pool. They shared a short load test: 200 reqs/second for 10s -> large % of requests returned 429, but some succeeded.

omar: likely NAT pooling. Important detail: IP-based limits are evaluated alongside auth-based limits on the platform. Even if a key has quota left, a shared NAT IP can hit an IP quota and cause 429s for all keys sharing that IP. Can we confirm whether they have org/node-level IP caps configured?

kevin: a bit more on scope precedence from infra side: quota checks go like this (simplified): 1) If authenticated, check API-key-specific quotas (most specific). 2) If not exhausted, we then evaluate project quotas and org quotas as fallbacks. 3) Separately, IP-address-based enforcement (NAT pools) runs as an additional constraint and can reject requests even if key/project/org quotas look fine. So IP checks can effectively surface a 429 that points to an "ip" scope.

maria: can you ask them to paste the raw response headers from a failing req? we look for something like `x-rw-quota-scope: ip|key|project|org` and the request id. that header will tell us which quota triggered the 429. also need timestamp range and the NAT IP list.

ian_support: Asked customer for raw headers and times. They sent one failing header blob: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`, `x-rw-quota-scope: ip`, `x-rw-quota-name: nat-pool-3`, `x-rw-limit: 500`, `x-rw-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-reset-ts: 2141590400`, `x-rw-request-id: rw_abc123`.

omar: confirms IP quota triggered — that matches NAT pool saturation. Repro recipe we suggest to customer (small script):

for i in {1..300}; do \
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-adverve-prod-01" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 52.18.23.$((i%5+1))" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &\
done

omar: If the NAT proxy collapses multiple origin IPs into a single NAT, the IP quota will be hit quickly.

kevin: mitigation options: 1) short-term: request we temporarily raise the IP quota for their org / NAT pool (we can do this for customers under support SLA). 2) advise the customer to preserve distinct source IPs or pass through client IPs in a way our edge will see them as separate (we require proper X-Forwarded-For preserved and trust chain from their proxy). 3) long-term: switch them to Reserved Dedicated or Private where IP-level isolation or per-customer egress is guaranteed.

maria: also note edge case — if a request omits Authorization (or Authorization is malformed), the system will only evaluate IP scopes and not apply per-key allowances. ask them to confirm the Authorization header is exactly as above and not being stripped.

ian_support: they confirmed Authorization header is present and the same key that succeeds from other IPs. Provided a failing request id and time window; asked for temporary IP quota bump.

kevin: I can run a quick lookup on the request id and time range to show which quota rule fired and whether the key itself had remaining quota. assigning to me, will post back with logs in ~20m.

maria: thanks. FYI I'll also send them a short checklist to reduce blast radius: 1) ensure proxy forwards X-Forwarded-For and does not rewrite it to a single static IP; 2) if using autoscaled runners, try staggering bursts across different nat pools; 3) if possible rotate to per-instance API keys so bursts don't concentrate on one key+ip pair.

ian_support: customer okay with temporary bump while infra investigates. I pinged them that we'll follow up with a timeline.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-214159-01 (support -> infra) assigned to kevin. priority: P2.

kevin: quick update — lookup shows `nat-pool-3` IP quota hit at 2141590389, api key had ~200 reqs remaining at that time. So root cause: NAT pool exhaustion. Will propose +1000 burst allowance for 6 hours and monitor.

maria: perfect. I'll close the loop with the customer and recommend the configuration checklist. :thumbsup:
